To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in the anaphylactic lungs of guinea pigs, thromboxane A2 is formed in large quantities but that the major part of this compound is inactivated by the formation of the inactive metabolite 15-keto-thromboxane A2.
in anaphlytic guinea pig lungs a major fraction of total thromboxane release is in the form biologically inactive 13, 14 dihydro-15 keto-thromboxane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of thromboxanes and prostaglandines in the pathogenesis of anaphylaxis and asthma.
the role of the cyclo-oxygense product thromboxane A2 in the anaphylactic response of the guinea pig heart and lung.
the development and application of specific radioimmunoassays for the determination of thromboxane and prostaglandine in biological fluids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thromboxane system, in particular the 15-keto metabolite of thromboxane, plays a significant role in anaphylactically induced bronchial constriction.
the anaphylactic reaction in guinea pig lungs involves both the thromboxane A2 and prostagladin D2 pathways.

the thromboxane A2 and prostaglanin D2 are both involved in the pathophysiological events in anaphylatic guinea-pig lungs, but that thromboxane B 2 and 15-keto 13,14-dihydrothromboxane B 1 are not involved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the anaphylactic lung is a major source of 15-ketodihydrothromboxane B 2 and prostaglanin D 2, which may contribute to the pathogenesis of anaphylaxis.
the thromboxanes and the prostaglandins are the most important mediators for anaphylactic shock.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 15-keto metabolite of thromboxane is a major product of the anaphylactic response in guinea pig lungs.

the use of a specific radioimmunoassays for 15-ketoprostaglandins is a valuable tool to investigate thromboxane metabolism in anaphylatic guinea pig lungs and to determine the role of thromboxane A2 and 15-ketodihydrothromboxane A2 in anaphylaxic shock.
15-keto-TXB2 and PGD2 are released in large amounts during anaphylactic lung contraction and that these two metabolites may contribute to the vascular and bronchospastic effects of anaphylaxis.
